key_insight: The anomalous γ-loop in Fe–Cr alloys arises from competing magnetic, vibrational and chemical effects that make chromium favor different crystal phases depending on temperature and composition.
engineering_relevance: Capturing these coupled effects can improve predictions of fcc–bcc phase stability for Fe–Cr alloy design and thermal processing.
method: Couple atomistic spin dynamics with ab initio molecular dynamics.
Use thermodynamic integration to calculate fcc–bcc Gibbs free-energy differences.
Compare magnetically ordered and disordered states to isolate magnetic contributions.
evidence_signal: Simulations at 0, 5, 10 and 15 at.% Cr over 800–1800 K reproduce the γ-loop’s compositional trend, with near-quantitative γ–δ transition agreement but α–γ temperatures underestimated by about 200 K.
watch_item: The α–γ boundary remains only qualitatively reproduced, and chemical clustering is a proposed—not established—explanation for the loop closing from below.
paper_title: Origin of the anomalous shape of the $γ$-loop in paramagnetic Fe1-xCrx alloys from coupled Atomistic Spin Dynamics and ab initio Molecular Dynamics
